therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: amyloid burden quantification as predictor of cognitive decline
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: subjects with prior florbetapir F 18 PET amyloid imaging with diagnoses of MCI, AD, or cognitively normal
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change in ADAS-Cog for MCI subjects at 36 months comparing amyloid-beta positive vs negative groups

results.effect_size: Aβ+ MCI: mean ADAS-Cog change +5.664; Aβ- MCI: mean ADAS-Cog change -0.710
results.target_engagement_evidence: Baseline global average SUVR correlated with 36-month ADAS-Cog change: r=0.502 (MCI), r=0.364 (AD), r=0.308 (CN)
biomarker_changes: Baseline SUVR correlated with 36-month ADAS-Cog change in MCI (r=0.502), AD (r=0.364), and CN (r=0.308)
Aβ+ MCI subjects showed greater decline across all psychometric measures vs Aβ- MCI
Aβ+ AD subjects showed mean ADAS-Cog change of +8.879 vs +3.811 for Aβ- AD
Aβ+ CN subjects showed mean ADAS-Cog change of +3.237 vs -0.094 for Aβ- CN
subgroup_findings: ADAS-Cog deterioration ≥4: 8 Aβ+ MCI vs 3 Aβ- MCI subjects
CDR deterioration ≥0.5: 5 Aβ+ MCI vs 4 Aβ- MCI subjects
Conversion to AD: 6 Aβ+ MCI vs 3 Aβ- MCI subjects
Conversion to CN: 1 Aβ+ MCI vs 5 Aβ- MCI subjects
ADAS-Cog deterioration ≥4: 14 Aβ+ AD vs 3 Aβ- AD subjects
CDR deterioration ≥0.5: 12 Aβ+ AD vs 2 Aβ- AD subjects
Aβ+ MCI showed greater DSS decline (-10.940) vs Aβ- MCI (0.133)
Aβ+ MCI showed greater CDR-SOB worsening (1.985) vs Aβ- MCI (0.392)
Aβ+ MCI showed greater MMSE decline (-2.882) vs Aβ- MCI (-0.300)
safety_signals: One serious adverse event of influenza reported in MCI group (1/36)

context.indication: Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment
context.comparator: amyloid-beta negative subjects (within each diagnostic group)
